card.name: Small linking words after a noun
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as in, of and those that come right after a noun or comma and begin a phrase about that noun. Seen in drug-label prose about studies, effects or patient groups.

modes.label: in / of after a noun
modes.description: A preposition follows a noun like studies, effects or support and introduces what it applies to.
modes.example: Because toxic effects<< of>> caffeine occur in very high dosages only

modes.label: in whom / in which after a comma
modes.description: The word in follows a comma and starts a relative clause about patients or studies.
modes.example: ROCKLATAN should be used with caution in aphakic patients,<< in>> pseudophakic patients with a torn

modes.label: those as a stand-in
modes.description: The word those replaces a repeated noun such as side effects when comparing two drugs.
modes.example: are generally rare and apparently independent of dose;<< those>> of hydrochlorothiazide are a
